items.text: Omar: Okay so, trial length for the launch, I've been thinking about this all weekend, and honestly I also finally watched that documentary about, never mind. I think we do a fourteen day free trial, no credit card needed. Sofia: No card at all? Omar: No card. The thing about cards is, nobody wants to type one in for a product they haven't tried. And that's what, like, kills signups. So if we drop that, more teams get in, they actually see it work, and I'd bet conversion to paid goes up. Nadia: I think maybe that's what, um, Slack and those companies did? Early on?

items.speaker: several speakers
items.text: Sofia: So for a month there's no check. Omar: It's a launch, you accept some noise. Sofia: I'm just flagging. Diego: I hear it. Let's go with the fourteen day free trial, no card, for launch.

items.speaker: several speakers
items.text: Sofia: It's a lot. And I think this is exactly what I was worried about. A no-card trial attracts people who never meant to pay, and some who are just abusing it. Those fake signups cost us about eleven hundred dollars a month in compute, and they wreck the funnel numbers, so we can't even tell what real conversion is. We need a card up front. Omar: Eleven hundred a month is nothing next to what we'd lose if- Sofia: It's nothing now. It's launch. Nadia: Could, um, email verification fix some of it?

items.speaker: several speakers
items.text: Diego: Okay. Trial policy again. Having looked at the signup drop and the enterprise prospects that fell out at the card step, I think we should reopen it. Marco: The cohort conversion came in. Eight point four percent, up from three point one. Sofia: See? Higher conversion. Marco: On a much smaller base. Total paid conversions are lower than before. Eleven, versus about fifty-nine.

items.speaker: several speakers
items.text: Aisha: He did, that's fine. But then he mentioned something I really didn't expect, and he said it like it was old news. Ravi: Uh oh. Aisha: The module we picked, the bundled one, they stop supporting it at the end of this year. After December there are no security patches for it, none. Camila: Wait, none? For something that would be handling payment approvals?

items.speaker: several speakers
items.text: Aisha: They're always slow. Greta: Stefan said last time it took them three weeks. Pavel: That was a software licence, this is a renewal. Should be quicker. Kofi: I think maybe they'll want the new quote though, since the old one's from March.

items.speaker: several speakers
items.text: Pavel: That was a software licence, this is a renewal. Should be quicker. Kofi: I think maybe they'll want the new quote though, since the old one's from March. Pavel: Probably. Okay. Is anyone sitting on an objection that we haven't heard? Greta: No. I'm fine. I wanted the free one, but the numbers aren't there.

items.speaker: several speakers
items.text: Lena: Yes, good, Insights. Meera: We launch September 9th, that's 33 days, and the pricing page has a gap where the trial line goes. Marketing asked me again yesterday. Lena: There's a whole bigger thing here, right, about how people first meet this tier, and whether it feels like- Yuki: Sorry, sorry, is it even settled that there's a trial? Because I've seen it in the draft copy and I never-

items.speaker: several speakers
items.text: Meera: Dana in IT. I'll ask her after this. Okay, Insights, because Pavel sent me something last night that I'd like everybody to hear. Lena: Is this the preview thing? Meera: The waitlist preview, yes. Marketing opened it last Thursday on the two-week terms, no card, so we've got seven days of real data. Pavel. Pavel: First week, 412 signups. 2.1 percent activated. 31 percent of accounts used disposable email addresses. Compute is 1.80 dollars per trial account.

items.speaker: several speakers
items.text: Jonas: I didn't say you were right, I said it's annoying. Lena: It does sort of hurt, the no-strings thing. I liked that. We're switching Insights to the 30-day trial with a card required at signup. Jonas: Noted, under protest, for the record.
